title: Differentialschrift: gemeinsame Lautfolge aus zustandsabhängigen Schriftänderungen
summary: RAW_UNSCREENED submission, then primary-reviewed strategic nomination: the written whole group may be a carrier state and a stable transformation from the previous group may encode a sound or syllable. Develop a complete hypothetical language reading together with one forward writing contract, rather than assigning meanings to whole surface groups. No decipherment experiment executed.

design.source_observation: Exposed f83r.4 has chedy qokedy; f83r.20 has qokeey qokedy. These are post-exposure illustrations, not evidence for the proposed channel. Full scope is all seven existing records, 51 lines, 341 groups.
design.mechanism: One state-dependent transformation has one shared hypothesized sound/syllable value across different carrier states; a whole visible group need not have one plaintext value.
design.discriminator: The same bounded operation-language contract must support complete linked statements and regenerate all visible groups, with seeds, segmentation choices and literals exposed. Reversibility, compression and local similarity alone do not distinguish meaning from re-encoding or message-free copying.
design.scope_limits: Only exposed W92 f83r projection for first block; reserves and f84/f84r sealed; no inherited glosses, legacy decoder repair, new corpus or external contact.
design.budget: First reading block about 90 minutes including formulation, implementation if needed, checking and publication; 20-minute checkpoint before substantial software. No new global time limit.
design.risk: Any text admits a lossless delta representation. Free replacement literals, ambiguous edit paths, free resets or unconstrained sound mappings can make an apparent reading tautological. No exhaustive novelty claim. Exact operational alphabet and language contract still need formulation before evaluation.
